what_it_does: Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) is an AI approach that represents information as very long binary vectors (hypervectors — imagine a string of tens of thousands of 0s and 1s) and makes decisions by comparing the similarity of these vectors. A key requirement is that the vectors assigned to different concepts must be nearly orthogonal to each other (mathematically unrelated), but finding such vectors traditionally requires an expensive search through all existing vectors — work that scales linearly with how many vectors you already have. This paper proposes generating hypervectors on the fly using a mathematical tool called the Hadamard transform (a structured pattern of +1 and -1 values arranged so that any two rows are perfectly orthogonal), which guarantees orthogonality in constant time with no search needed. The scheme is implemented in hardware using in-memory computing — doing the math directly inside the memory chip rather than shuttling data back and forth — and simplifies the encoding step to additions only, making the chip compact and fast.
